original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC's displayed maximum concurrent-session policy equals the required per-service matrix—KVM 2, Redfish 20, SSH 5, Virtual Media 4 and Web 20—using authoritative GUI or vendor API fields for the exact firmware without modifying any policy.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT firmware and authorized read-only account; capture the Security and Access > Policies Max Session Service Information page; discover the canonical Redfish and vendor-extension resources; map each displayed service label to an exact resource/property and unit; collect complete secret-redacted responses; compare integer values 2/20/5/4/20 independently; record any missing/unsupported field instead of assuming zero or inferring from a generic SessionService limit; close sessions without writes.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies the firmware-specific GUI/API mapping and limit semantics; ordinary read-only browser/API collection is fully automatable.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware and authorized read-only account
Exact GUI labels and canonical Redfish/vendor resource/property for each service
Definition of maximum: configured cap, licensed cap, simultaneous active sessions or per-user limit
Required matrix KVM=2, Redfish=20, SSH=5, Virtual Media=4, Web=20 and any firmware/SKU exceptions
safety_requirements: Use only GET/browser read actions and verify the exact BMC
Validate TLS or approved trust; keep credentials/tokens out of command lines and evidence
Preserve complete resources and GUI values without filtering away property context
Treat missing, null, duplicate or differently scoped values as unresolved/mismatch rather than pass
Do not PATCH limits, terminate sessions, reset BMC or clear logs
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, schema/property mapping and expected matrix
Collect read-only GUI/API evidence and compare all five services independently
Report absent/ambiguous/vendor-only fields without inventing mappings
Do not modify policies, assume generic MaxConcurrentSessions applies to every service, disable TLS validation, expose secrets or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve per-service property/source and maximum-session semantics
Review any missing/mismatched value and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A SessionService GET is a useful discovery step but may expose only Redfish-session limits; it cannot be assumed to contain KVM, SSH, Virtual Media and Web caps. `-k` and inline basic credentials are unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a protected Redfish session to GET SessionService and documented vendor policy resources, plus automated GUI readback when needed, then compare each mapped integer to 2/20/5/4/20.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All five service labels/limits, GUI Policies path and 5/5-minute estimate remain exactly preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind each GUI service limit to a firmware-versioned API/property or captured DOM field and validate the five-value matrix independently with raw provenance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds schema discovery, GUI/API cross-reference, maximum semantics, secure session handling and per-field result separation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One generic SessionService MaxSessions value cannot represent five distinct protocols unless the vendor schema explicitly documents that mapping.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some limits may be compile-time/licensed GUI data rather than standard Redfish properties; browser DOM labels can change by firmware localization.

project_override_considerations: If no supported API exposes a service limit, authenticated GUI DOM/screenshot evidence is acceptable for that field; lack of API must not silently drop the GUI-required coverage. Session-cap enforcement under load is outside this read-only information case unless separately approved.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT firmware, account role and GUI Policies page timestamp
Complete redacted SessionService/vendor resources and/or DOM capture
Per-service GUI label to resource/property mapping and limit semantics
Independent comparisons: KVM 2, Redfish 20, SSH 5, Virtual Media 4, Web 20
Missing/ambiguous/mismatch list, no-write/session audit and engineer verdict

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2227 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00010-V001: approve the BMC/firmware/SKU-specific mapping from GUI KVM/Redfish/SSH/Virtual Media/Web labels to canonical Redfish or vendor properties (or GUI-only evidence), define whether each 2/20/5/4/20 value is a configured, licensed, simultaneous or per-user maximum, document exceptions and approve TLS/secret-safe read-only access.

review_improvement: Keeps safe full automation while preventing a generic SessionService response from falsely covering five distinct GUI policies and preserving exact per-field provenance.
independent_technical_reasoning: Redfish SessionService defines session behavior for Redfish sessions, while KVM, SSH, virtual media and Web often have separate vendor policy controls. Therefore five limits cannot be derived from one property without a documented extension. The source provides exact integers, so the automation can deterministically compare them once each value's provenance and scope are mapped. All actions are reads, so no confirmation is required and no policy should be changed merely to make displayed values match.
